beats.hook: My neighbor called the city on me seventeen times in one year. So I spent three weeks making sure she'd never bother anyone again.
beats.the_wrong: Sandra had lived next door for six years and treated our street like her personal HOA dictatorship. She reported me for a trash can that was two inches past my property line, a wind chime she called a noise hazard, and a garden hose I left out on a Tuesday. Each complaint cost me time, money, and my sanity.
beats.the_plan: Turns out Sandra was running an unlicensed daycare out of her house — eleven kids, no permit, no inspection. I know because she bragged about it at the block party two summers ago. So I started documenting. Every car, every drop-off time, every visible head count through her front window.
beats.the_execution: I filed one single complaint with the county licensing board, attached forty-three photos, three weeks of handwritten logs, and a noise recording of fourteen children screaming at eight in the morning. The inspector showed up on a Wednesday. Sandra answered the door in her robe. I watched from my porch, drinking coffee.
beats.the_satisfaction: She had to shut it down within ten days. Eleven families scrambling, zero sympathy from me. The wind chime is still hanging. I bought a second one.
beats.cta: Follow for more stories and drop in the comments what you would have done differently.
